title: A Review of Small Language Models for Code and Domain-Specific Language Artifact Generation
content: Small Language Models (SLMs, up to 7B parameters) offer a resource-efficient alternative to large models for code generation tasks, yet existing studies of their application to domain-specific languages (DSLs) use heterogeneous task formulations and evaluation protocols. This paper reviews SLMs for DSL artifact generation, including configurations, security policies, and infrastructure templates. Based on an analysis of the literature, we propose a classification of DSL artifact generation tasks according to the composition of the required context model. Classes C1–C3 represent a progression from local structural constraints to schema and inter-element relationships and then to dependencies on semantics and the execution environment. For these classes, we formulate hypotheses about model adaptation strategies. We systematize adaptation methods, including LoRA/QLoRA, distillation, grammar-constrained decoding, and RAG, and highlight automatic formal verification as a key advantage of DSLs for reliable generation in critical infrastructure settings.
